subject: I prefer Aussi rules
author: SUFFUR
body:
Fast and as violent as both games of Rugby and American Football. But at least when you go to any of these games(all three) you don't get a riot at the end of the match, or bad crowd control issuses, unlike English Football, and no riots at the end of a 'sockar' (as they play in socks)game either. I played both games of, Rugby, Right Hook or Fly Forward (you know, i could be making this up?) and Quarter Back, in American Football ( i was tallish, skinny, but fast and fit, and a target, so i had to run), and have to say both are fun and just as hard hitting. But played Football for a Sunday League and broke more bones in the 2 years i played, (though i still played with said breakages till the end of the match, in the other sports, you get hit bad, your in a coma or stretchered out to a medica facitiy near by, it does happen in English Football, but normally for some very nasty leg injuries, no details some of them were just gross), the team was pretty poor so not a lot of players on the side lines, but was a fun way to keep fit with your mates, alas i found XBox Live a few years after, and they have gone on to better things, NOT!

PS, have never played Aussi Rules and have watched a dozen or more games, and still don't understand it? But they look fit, don't stop running, and they do, what is very wierd things to the ball, sort of a volly ball punt, forward, and off course kick it. I think the origins of all football games are a variant of some sort of object passed round, even a head of a foe, and placed into goals of sorts, or a spike at the end of the field. Its nice to see sport on peoples agenda, what ever variant it is. And I hope all your teams every success, in the future. But go Wales(yes Boot, my friend is a big fan, so i give support), the All Blacks, my team of choice, Newcastle, (me Dads a Gordie), the Cowboys, (sorry have been a fan for 30 years) and the Chicargo Bulls, as i was knoob to basket ball and i watched a lot of thier games, though the Harlem GlobeTroters, were my first basketball, live viewing, and prefered that style of play, until i was told it was a form of entertainment? Is not all sport now, with the amount of money spent, entertainment? And as for College Ball, i have a lot to learn, as all I know, people are watching for the next big player to come up the ranks to be a Pro, piece of entertainment and the good life with a huge pay cheque, and you saw them rise from the proving ground to stardom. It's good to watch!

Patience is something I taught myself, so I never know when it's going to run out?
